summary: Build practical PDNA, recovery planning, and monitoring skills. Explore the five-day course and strengthen your recovery work.
lede: Disaster recovery training prepares recovery practitioners, programme managers, and technical specialists to assess impacts and coordinate recovery priorities. It covers damage and loss assessment, needs prioritization, and planning to restore essential services, housing, infrastructure, and livelihoods. Participants practise building a prioritized needs matrix, setting reconstruction priorities, and monitoring progress with an Excel dashboard, using the PDNA methodology and Sendai Framework as references.
audienceIntro: This intermediate course is designed for professionals who assess disaster impacts, coordinate recovery programmes, restore services, or report on reconstruction progress. This course is designed for: Post-Disaster Recovery Coordinator managing multi-sector recovery priorities and delivery. PDNA Assessment Specialist consolidating damage, loss, and recovery needs evidence. Disaster Recovery Programme Manager linking recovery plans to budgets and milestones. Resilient Infrastructure Engineer prioritizing safer repair and reconstruction projects. Housing Recovery Officer coordinating shelter transition and permanent housing recovery. Livelihoods Recovery Specialist assessing household and market recovery needs. Humanitarian Coordination Officer connecting relief activities with recovery planning. Community Engagement and Accountability Officer tracking feedback in recovery decisions. Recovery Monitoring and Evaluation Officer maintaining outcome indicators and progress reports. Public Finance or Donor Programme Officer reviewing recovery allocations and implementation evidence.
prerequisites: Working familiarity with disaster response, humanitarian programmes, development, public services, or infrastructure recovery is recommended. No coding or programming is required. Bring a laptop with Excel access for spreadsheet-based exercises; no specialist software is required.
